_readme: Text for the Research page. Project cards on that page come from projects.json (category: research).
lede: My research is about making learned perception dependable enough to act on. I work on detectors and trackers that drive physical systems, video models that learn the structure of a scene, and the benchmarks and calibration methods needed to know when either can be trusted.

areas.title: Vision for production systems and digital twins
areas.text: Fine-tuned object detection, multi-object tracking, and multi-camera live inference that keep a virtual production line in step with the physical one, and close the loop back to a robot arm.

areas.title: Video world models and self-supervised learning
areas.text: Object-centric joint-embedding predictive models (JEPA) for video, with training curricula that focus on the objects a model finds hardest to predict.

areas.title: Benchmarks, calibration, and evaluation
areas.text: Benchmark construction with calibration and held-out splits, comparisons against tuned statistical baselines, and conformal prediction for alarm thresholds and decision guarantees.

areas.title: Learned monitoring of quantum error-correction streams
areas.text: Treating syndrome measurements as sparse binary video, so that a video transformer can track noise drift, and testing that idea against classical estimators and on real hardware recordings.

areas.title: Reliable memory systems
areas.text: Earlier work on error-correcting codes that tolerate multiple cell upsets with low overhead.

directions: Extending the closed-loop digital twin for production lines, where perception latency, tracking quality, and manipulation success are measured stage by stage on live hardware.
Hard-example curricula for video world models, building on difficulty-ranked masking.
Learned and hybrid monitors for drifting signal streams, with alarm rates calibrated on held-out data.
Collaborative work on conformal prediction and calibrated decisions for surgical video and ordinal medical imaging.

methodology.title: Build the benchmark first
methodology.text: Datasets with explicit train, validation, calibration, and test splits, held-out conditions, and ground-truth labels, so that claims can be checked.

methodology.title: Compare against tuned baselines
methodology.text: Controlled comparisons with strong statistical baselines, ablations, multiple seeds, and paired significance tests such as McNemar's.

methodology.title: Calibrate, then decide
methodology.text: Thresholds set with conformal prediction and verified against target false-alarm rates on held-out data.

methodology.title: Validate after deployment
methodology.text: Latency measured on live streams, end-to-end task success on real hardware, and per-camera and stage-wise error slicing to find where failures actually come from.

achievements: First author of three papers under review: CVPR 2027, IEEE ICRA 2027, and IEEE ICASSP 2027.
Co-author of a published paper at ICICN 2026 and an accepted paper at IEEE SMC 2026.
IEEE conference paper from undergraduate thesis work (ICECIT 2021).
